prompt: A dental practice's patient visits grew 8%, but profit fell 10%. It hired two hygienists last year. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The new hygienists probably added cost faster than they added visits.
options.feedback: Right. Visits grew 8% but two salaries were added. I'd compare visits per hygienist before and after the hires.

options.text: Patients are likely drifting to a rival that opened nearby.
The practice overhired and needs to let one hygienist go.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain and jumps to a fix before any data.

options.text: Insurers have likely cut what they pay per visit.
options.feedback: Possible, but nothing points to it. The change the prompt gives is the two new hires.

explanation: The data shows visits up 8% but profit down 10% after two hygienists were hired. Likely cause: the hires added cost faster than visits. To test it, compare visits per hygienist before and after. If productivity held, look at insurer payments or supply costs.
